overview: After 1.g3 d5 2.Nf3 Black throws in ...g5, offering a pawn and a big kingside weakening. White normally takes with 3.Nxg5 and plays Bg2 and d4 or c4, with a healthy extra pawn while Black seeks activity down the g-file and with ...Bg7-type play.

white_ideas.idea: Take the g5 pawn with Nxg5 and consolidate with Bg2, d3 or d4
Use the open g-file and the weak Black kingside

black_ideas.idea: Regain the pawn or get piece activity with ...Bg7... and ...e5
Use the central pawns d5 and e5

typical_structures.structure: Black h-pawn and g-pawn missing, White fianchetto against a central ...d5/...e5 duo

character.notes: A pawn sacrifice at move two with an exposed Black king gives unbalanced, forcing play. Black wild at move two, White keeps a pawn.

gambit.notes: White can simply take 3.Nxg5 and keep the pawn.

soundness.notes: Black gets little for the pawn against sensible play.

structure.notes: Centre not committed; pieces and flank pawns decide.

approach.notes: Seldom seen from strong players on either side.

level.notes: Dubious lines are never Beginner; White needs only sound development.
